module purpose: neorv32_wdt holds a bus-written control setting (enable, lock, strict, 24-bit timeout), counts prescaler ticks taken from clkgen_i in cnt while enabled, restarts the count only on a write of the constant password reset_pwd_c, and drives a reset request on rstn_o when the count equals the timeout or, in strict mode, when an illegal access occurs; it records the cause of the last reset in reset_cause, returns settings and cause on bus reads, and exports the enable on clkgen_en_o.

use-case flows.value: enable, strict and timeout settings taken from bus write data at addr(2)='0' while unlocked, held in ctrl and exported (enable) on clkgen_en_o
ctrl.lock, settable only while ctrl.enable is '1'; once set it blocks every ctrl write, a write attempt raises reset_force, and only rstn_sys_i clears it
watchdog restart request: a write at addr(2)='1' whose data equals reset_pwd_c sets reset_wdt, which clears cnt; any other data raises reset_force
timeout counting: prescaler tick from clkgen_i, start flag cnt_started, increment strobe cnt_inc, counter cnt cleared when disabled or restarted, and comparison of cnt with ctrl.timeout
watchdog reset request: timeout reset (hw_rst_timeout) and strict-mode access-violation reset (hw_rst_access) combined onto rstn_o
reset cause code recorded in reset_cause with priority debug reset, then timeout, then access violation
ctrl.enable, ctrl.lock, reset_cause, ctrl.strict and ctrl.timeout returned on bus_rsp_o.data on a read strobe
rstn_sys_i low clears ctrl, reset_wdt, reset_force, cnt, cnt_inc, cnt_started, hw_rst_timeout and hw_rst_access; only rstn_ext_i low clears reset_cause

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog enable setting -- whether the watchdog counts and may raise any reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.enable is written by `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_enable_c);` (line 94) only when unlocked (GATED_BY ctrl.lock, line 93) and held between writes (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3). Its value decides the whole watchdog: '0' clears cnt (GATES cnt, line 131), it qualifies cnt_started (line 130), both reset requests (GATES hw_rst_timeout line 155, GATES hw_rst_access line 156), and whether lock can be set (GATES ctrl.lock, line 95). Integrity is Established: a wrong enable would suppress or allow counting and reset generation contrary to these lines. It leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o by `clkgen_en_o <= ctrl.enable;` (line 140, COPIES ctrl.enable), so under the boundary-integrity assumption the consumer must receive exactly this value. Availability is also Established: the setting is held until rewritten or cleared by rstn_sys_i (line 75). Readback at line 109 goes through bus_rsp_o, a transport record, so it is not an exit reference; the setting value enters through bus_req_i.data, also transport, so no sets reference survives.

conceptual assets.concept: Configuration lock -- the state that freezes the watchdog settings until system reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: The lock flow: `ctrl.lock <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_lock_c) and ctrl.enable;` (line 95) sets the lock only while the watchdog is enabled; `if (ctrl.lock = '0') then` (line 93, GATES ctrl.enable, ctrl.lock, ctrl.strict, ctrl.timeout at occurrence 3) blocks every settings write once set, including a write that would clear the lock itself, and the else arm raises reset_force (line 99, GATES reset_force). Only rstn_sys_i clears it (line 76, RESET_BY). Integrity is Established: a corrupted lock would let enable, strict and timeout be changed, or would turn legal writes into access violations. ctrl.lock stores this state (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 95). Its readback (line 110) uses the transport record bus_rsp_o and is not an exit reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Strict mode setting -- whether an illegal access produces a reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.strict is written by `ctrl.strict <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_strict_c);` (line 96) while unlocked and held (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3). It decides the access-violation reset: `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force;` (line 156, GATES hw_rst_access at occurrence 5). Integrity is Established: a wrong value would drop or invent the reset that the RTL produces for a write while locked (line 99) or a wrong password (line 105). It is a held setting, so it realizes its own concept although it also gates hw_rst_access. Readback (line 112) is through the transport record bus_rsp_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout threshold -- the count at which the watchdog expires
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.timeout is written by `ctrl.timeout <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_timeout_msb_c downto ctrl_timeout_lsb_c);` (line 97) while unlocked and held (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3). The expiry decision compares it with the count: `cnt_timeout <= '1' when (cnt_started = '1') and (cnt = ctrl.timeout) else '0';` (line 144, CONSTRAINS cnt_timeout at occurrence 5). Integrity is Established: a corrupted threshold moves or prevents the timeout reset of line 155. Availability is also Established: the threshold is held until rewritten or cleared by rstn_sys_i (line 78). Readback (line 113) is through the transport record bus_rsp_o.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog count state -- the elapsed-tick count and the started flag that qualify expiry
conceptual assets.reasoning: cnt is a self-updating counter (flow graph): `cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(cnt) + 1);` (line 134, DERIVES_FROM cnt, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4) when cnt_inc is '1' (line 133), and cleared when ctrl.enable is '0' or reset_wdt is '1' (lines 131-132). cnt_started is a self-updating state flag: `cnt_started <= ctrl.enable and (cnt_started or prsc_tick);` (line 130, CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 4); it qualifies increments (line 129) and the expiry decision (GATES cnt_timeout, line 144). Integrity is Established: the expiry comparison at line 144 is only correct if cnt counts exactly the qualified ticks since the last restart. Availability holds only under the RTL conditions (enable '1', started, ticks arriving); no external tick rate is assumed. cnt_inc is a one-cycle registered increment strobe that only gates cnt (GATES cnt, line 133), and prsc_tick only forwards a bit of clkgen_i (line 141); neither is reported. clkgen_i supplies the prescaler tick that enables counting and reset sampling (lines 129, 141, 155), acting as a clock-enable input, so it is not reported.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog restart authorization -- the decision that a write carried the exact restart password
conceptual assets.reasoning: The restart flow: `if (bus_req_i.data(31 downto 0) = reset_pwd_c) then reset_wdt <= '1';` (lines 102-103, GATED_BY bus_req_i.data at occurrence 4), else reset_force (line 105). reset_wdt is a pulse cleared every cycle (line 87) and it clears the counter (GATES cnt, occurrence 5, line 131). Integrity is Established: a corrupted decision would restart the count without the password, defeating expiry, or refuse a valid restart and let the timeout reset fire. reset_wdt stores the decision for one cycle (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4, line 103); stores is preferred over computes. The password value reset_pwd_c is a constant, not a candidate, and bus_req_i is transport, so no other reference survives. Confidentiality of the password is context-dependent and not claimed.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout expiry and timeout reset request -- the decision that the count reached the threshold and the reset it triggers
conceptual assets.reasoning: cnt_timeout computes the expiry decision at line 144 (CONSTRAINED_BY cnt and ctrl.timeout, GATED_BY cnt_started, occurrence 2). `hw_rst_timeout <= ctrl.enable and cnt_timeout and prsc_tick;` (line 155) registers the reset request (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3), which drives `rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access);` (line 161, DERIVES_FROM at occurrence 2) and selects cause code 10 (GATES reset_cause, line 173). Integrity is Established: the reset must assert exactly when enabled, started and cnt equals ctrl.timeout at a tick. Availability is Established under those conditions: the RTL requires the request to be produced when they hold. rstn_o carries the value out of the entity, so the boundary-integrity assumption applies to it. The map lists cnt_timeout as not reached from a source because its inputs are control edges; the RTL line 144 shows its computation.

conceptual assets.concept: Illegal access event and access-violation reset request -- a settings write while locked or a wrong restart password, and the strict-mode reset it triggers
conceptual assets.reasoning: reset_force is set to '1' by a settings write while locked (line 99, GATED_BY ctrl.lock at occurrence 4) or by a restart write whose data differs from reset_pwd_c (line 105, GATED_BY bus_req_i.data at occurrence 5), and cleared every other cycle (line 88); it stores this decision (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4). `hw_rst_access <= ctrl.enable and ctrl.strict and reset_force;` (line 156) registers the reset request (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 3), which drives rstn_o (line 161, DERIVES_FROM hw_rst_access at occurrence 2) and cause code 11 (GATES reset_cause, line 175). Integrity is Established: the illegal-access detection and the reset must follow lines 93-105 and 156. Availability is Established under the RTL conditions (enable and strict '1'). rstn_o is the exit port of this decision.

conceptual assets.concept: Reset cause record -- which event caused the last reset
conceptual assets.reasoning: reset_identifier records the cause with fixed priority: rstn_dbg_i low gives 01 (line 172), else hw_rst_timeout gives 10 (line 174), else hw_rst_access gives 11 (line 176); reset_cause stores it (CLOCKED_BY clk_i, occurrence 4). It is cleared only by rstn_ext_i (lines 168-169, RESET_BY), not by rstn_sys_i, which clears every other register (lines 73, 124, 151), so the record is preserved across a system reset. Integrity is Established: the reported cause (read at line 111) must match the event that occurred. rstn_dbg_i is an input this entity reads to decide the code (GATES reset_cause, occurrence 2, line 171); it drives no SEQUENCES or RESETS here, so the reset-input exclusion does not apply and it sets the concept. Readback goes through the transport record bus_rsp_o and is not an exit reference.
